provenance.note: Place name on the river, geocoded to the reach [supplied on this invocation]
Steady upstream discharge - the flow whose depth and travel time set how much heat the reach picks up per kilometre [supplied on this invocation]

First day of the observed weather the reach is driven over, 'YYYY-MM-DD' - from phrasing like 'last week' or 'the first week of August'. The station record is hourly and the network holds the last two weeks, so an earlier day refuses typed [supplied on this invocation]

Last day of the observed weather, 'YYYY-MM-DD'. The run is sim_duration_s long from the first observation, so this day has to be far enough past weather_start to cover it; at most 14 days after [supplied on this invocation]

Where the temperature series and its diurnal range are read, as a Point: the pick's {coordinates, name} verbatim, a (lon, lat) pair, 'lat,lon', a point layer, or a place name [supplied on this invocation]
Result-writing cadence; unset keeps the steering file's own period [supplied on this invocation]
Modelled reach length downstream of the geocoded point; the water warms with the time it spends in the reach, so the length is how much exposure the question asks about [supplied on this invocation]

Simulated time. A DIURNAL RANGE needs whole days, and this defaults to seven; a shorter run answers what the reach did over that window and no more. The weather record has to span every second of it - a run longer than its own forcing refuses rather than extrapolating [supplied on this invocation]
Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; a surface heat budget is a reach-scale answer, so this is coarser than a plume question asks for [supplied on this invocation]
not supplied; the reach flowline is fetched fresh for the AOI
not supplied; the carrier discharge is read at the MOST RECENT published NWM cycle

not supplied; the reach opens at the water temperature the nearest USGS / EPA Water Quality Portal sample site reports, with that site and its sample date on the provenance note; no sample site refuses typed rather than opening at a guessed temperature
not supplied; the reach is solved at Strickler 33.0, which is also the roughness its outflow stage is derived as a normal depth at
not supplied; the coefficient is read as a Strickler one

answer.discharge_note: Steady upstream discharge - the flow whose depth and travel time set how much heat the reach picks up per kilometre [supplied on this invocation]
answer.mesh_resolution_note: Target element edge length the reach is triangulated at; a surface heat budget is a reach-scale answer, so this is coarser than a plume question asks for [supplied on this invocation]
